notes: face.ba is WordPress 7.1.3 behind the Hummingbird cache plugin. robots.txt is HTTP 404 on both face.ba and www.face.ba, so polite_fetch records it as assumed_open and nothing is disallowed. Every sitemap route I probed is 404: /sitemap.xml, /wp-sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /news-sitemap.xml, /sitemap-news.xml (all HTTP 404, empty body), so there is no sitemap at all and no per-day/per-month sitemap to use. /feed/ and /rss are HTTP 200 but serve only ~10 items per page, which is lossy (a previous feed-paged run produced 1105 URLs and only 9 for 2026-10-25 against 30 actually published that day). Section/date archive pages exist but are heavy HTML with paging. The route that works is the open WP REST API, one request per 100 posts: GET https://face.ba/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?per_page=100&page=N&after=2026-09-25T00:00:00&before=2026-10-26T00:00:00&orderby=date&order=desc&_fields=id,date,link -- HTTP 200, 17 pages of 100 plus a last page of 12, then HTTP 400 (page out of range) which ends the loop. 'date' is the site's own local publication timestamp (Europe/Sarajevo) and 'link' the canonical article URL; no date parsing or guessing is needed. Result: 1712 unique URLs over all 31 days in ~10 s, 2026-09-30=40, 2026-10-10=62, 2026-10-20=58. Verification: 13 articles re-fetched across 09-30, 10-05, 10-10, 10-11, 10-20 including the five with empty API content (video/dnevnik posts); each page's own article:published_time equals the listed date exactly, and stripped page text is 2837-7474 characters, so the 1500-character and +-1-day requirements hold even for the shortest posts (the site's nav/related boilerplate alone is ~2.8k characters). Everything goes through polite_fetch. Caveat for anyone reusing this: face.ba has no sitemap and the feed is lossy; use the REST API.
